title: Vietnamese Food in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Vietnamese food is part of everyday Berlin.** A Lichtenberg district study counted 36,473 residents with a Vietnamese migration reference in 2023, including 12,500 in Lichtenberg.
**The history crossed both sides of the Wall:** South Vietnamese refugees arrived in West Berlin from the late 1970s, while a 1980 agreement brought Vietnamese contract workers to the GDR.
**Choose the area by the evening:** Mitte for minimum travel, Kantstraße for several restaurants in one walk, and Kreuzberg for vegan-first options.
**Use Dong Xuan as a daytime market trip.** Take tram M8 to Herzbergstr./Dong-Xuan; the center publishes 10:00–20:00 Wednesday to Monday and Tuesday closed, while individual businesses vary.
**Start with one clear dish:** pho is noodle soup, bun is a rice-noodle bowl, banh mi is a baguette sandwich, and goi cuon are fresh summer rolls.
**Check the exact venue before travelling.** Menus, opening hours, reservations, language support and payment methods vary; carry a card plus some cash.
